title: zsh command history
whyItMatters: zsh is the default shell on modern macOS. Its history file can contain typed commands, paths and sometimes tokens or passwords.
source: zsh manual, HISTFILE (macOS default shell since Catalina writes ~/.zsh_history); macforensics.app cheat sheet (Shell History)
notes: Only existence, size and timestamps are recorded. Commands are never read. An extended history file under a custom HISTFILE is out of scope.

steps: Quit Terminal and any other terminal app so the history file is not written again.
Open the file named in the plan in a text editor and copy out any command you need to keep.
Delete the file, then empty the Trash, so the next shell starts with empty history.
cleanup.risk: Every command you typed is lost, including paths, server names or tokens typed by mistake.
cleanup.source: zsh manual, Parameters set by the shell (HISTFILE): https://zsh.sourceforge.net/Doc/Release/Parameters.html
